**Sikhae (Seaweed Soup) – A Quick & Easy Recipe** *This classic Korean dish is light, comforting, and perfect for a quick lunch or dinner. It’s usually served with rice and a side of kimchi.* --- ### Ingredients | Item | Amount | Notes | |------|--------|-------| | **Kelp (seaweed)** | 1 sheet (about 5 cm × 15 cm) | Fresh or dried; if dried, soak it first. | | **Water** | 2 cups (480 ml) | Use fresh tap water or filtered water. | | **Soy sauce** | 1 tablespoon | Adjust to taste. | | **Sesame oil** | 1 teaspoon | Adds aroma. | | **Garlic** | 1 clove, minced | Optional, for extra flavor. | | **Green onion** | 1 stalk, sliced | For garnish. | | **Optional add‑ins** | | • Tofu cubes
• Thinly sliced mushrooms
• Spinach or bok choy
• Scallion oil (for drizzling) | --- ### Equipment - Small pot or saucepan - Knife & cutting board - Measuring spoons --- ### Instructions 1. **Prepare the Kelp** - If you’re using dried kelp, rinse it under cold water, then soak it in 2 cups of water for about 10–15 minutes until it expands. - If you have fresh kelp, simply rinse it thoroughly to remove any grit. 2. **Cook the Base** - Place the soaked kelp (with its soaking water) into a small pot. - Bring to a gentle boil over medium heat. - Reduce the heat to low and let it simmer for **5–7 minutes**. The kelp will soften and release its umami flavor into the broth. 3. **Season the Broth** - Add soy sauce and sesame oil to the pot. Stir gently. - Taste the broth; if you prefer a saltier soup, add a pinch more soy sauce. - If you like garlic, stir in the minced garlic now and let it cook for an additional minute. 4. **Add Optional Ingredients** - If you’re adding tofu, mushrooms, or greens, toss them in at this point. - Let everything simmer together for another **2–3 minutes** until the vegetables are tender but still crisp. 5. **Finish & Serve** - Remove the pot from heat. - Ladle the soup into bowls. - Garnish each bowl with sliced green onions. - Drizzle a little scallion oil over the top if you have it, for extra fragrance. 6. **Enjoy** - Serve hot alongside steamed rice and a side of kimchi. - Sip slowly—this soup is meant to be savored! --- ### Tips & Variations - **Flavor Boost**: Add a splash of fish sauce or a pinch of sugar to balance the salty soy sauce. - **Protein Upgrade**: Replace tofu with thinly sliced beef or shrimp for a heartier meal. - **Texture Play**: Toss in some sliced carrots or zucchini for crunch. - **Make Ahead**: The broth can be made ahead and stored in the fridge for up to 2 days. Reheat gently before serving. Enjoy your homemade sikhae! If you’d like a more detailed version or variations, just let me know.
